sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the filter bar
sections.what: Brings in the React tools, the icons, the portfolio helper functions and the shared state hook.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the tools the bar needs to read filters and build labels.

sections.name: Select
sections.title: Reusable labeled dropdown
sections.what: Draws one labeled dropdown with an All option first. Its border turns red when a choice is picked, so the user can see an active filter.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared piece keeps all five dropdowns looking and behaving the same.
sections.watch_out: An empty value means All, so no real choice can use an empty value.

sections.name: FilterBar (part 1)
sections.title: Computing choices and active filter count
sections.what: Keeps the search text in step with the address and delays the address update while typing. Works out each dropdown's choices from the projects that match the other filters, and works out which industries are in scope. Counts the active filters for the phone button.
sections.why: Likely reason: narrowing each list by the other filters stops the user from picking a combination that gives no results.
sections.watch_out: A value picked in one dropdown can disappear from another dropdown's list, so that dropdown may look empty even though a filter is set.

sections.name: FilterBar (part 2)
sections.title: Search box, scope switch and dropdown layout
sections.what: Draws the search box, the Live versus All industries switch (all-industries page only), the phone Filters button, the Clear button when filters are set, and the grid of five dropdowns.
sections.why: Likely reason: the Filters button hides the dropdown grid on phones to save space. Other layout reasons are not stated.
sections.watch_out: The Clear button resets the industry, country, phase, segment, company and search, but not the scope switch, which users may expect it to reset.

summary: A search box and dropdown filters that narrow every portfolio view, with the choices kept in the web address.
purpose: Lets a user find projects by text and narrow them by industry, country, phase, segment and company, and shows how many filters are active.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Keeping the filters in the web address means any view shows the same narrowing and a filtered view can be shared by its address.
how: Reads the current filters and scope. For each dropdown, lists only the choices that still lead to matching projects after the other filters are applied. Works out which industries are in scope. Draws the search box, a Live versus All scope switch (on the all-industries page only), an industry dropdown (all-industries page only), four more dropdowns, a Filters button for phones, and a Clear button when any filter is set.
inputs: The portfolio data (industries and projects), the current filters from the web address, and the industry slug when a single industry is selected.
outputs: Updates to the web address when a filter is picked or typed, which makes every view re-draw with the narrowed set. A count of active filters appears on the phone Filters button.
risks: Typed search text is applied 250 milliseconds after typing stops, so there is a short delay. Changing one dropdown can remove a value that another dropdown still has selected, because each list is narrowed by the other filters. The clear timer for search is not cancelled if the bar disappears, so a late update can still change the address.
debug: If a dropdown shows no choices, check the filter call used for that dropdown and the data. If search does not update the view, check the timer and the sync from the address. If Clear leaves filters set, check the names of the parameters it clears. If the phone Filters button does nothing, check the open state.
